question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for protecting and improving the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 48-A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 48-A was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, as a Directive Principle of State Policy (Part IV). (अनुच्छेद 48-ए — पर्यावरण संरक्षण)

 

• It states: "The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country."

 

• It works in tandem with Article 51-A(g), a Fundamental Duty added by the same amendment, which casts a similar obligation on every citizen.

 

• This provision reflects India's commitment following the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including insertion of the words "Socialist" and "Secular" in the Preamble.

 

• Article 21 has also been judicially interpreted (e.g., in M.C. Mehta cases) to include the right to a healthy environment as part of the right to life.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 47-A (Option 1): Non-existent; Article 47 actually deals with the State's duty to raise the level of nutrition, standard of living and public health, and to bring about prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs.

 

• Article 47-B (Option 2): Non-existent — there is no such provision in the Constitution.

 

• Article 49-C (Option 4): Non-existent; Article 49 deals with the protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance.

question: According to Mendeleev's Periodic Table, which elements’ properties matched up remarkably well with eka-silicon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Germanium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev left a gap in his Periodic Table (1869) below silicon and predicted the properties of an undiscovered element, calling it "eka-silicon". (एका-सिलिकॉन — जर्मेनियम)

 

• The element was discovered in 1886 by German chemist Clemens Winkler and named Germanium, after Germany.

 

• Its predicted properties (atomic weight, density, colour, oxide behaviour) matched Winkler's findings remarkably closely, providing strong validation of Mendeleev's periodic law.

 

• Germanium is a metalloid widely used today as a semiconductor material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendeleev similarly predicted "eka-aluminium" (later identified as Gallium, discovered 1875) and "eka-boron" (later identified as Scandium, discovered 1879).

 

• The accurate prediction of these three elements was a major factor behind the general acceptance of the Periodic Table.

 

NOTE

 

• Gallium (Option 1): This corresponds to Mendeleev's "eka-aluminium", not eka-silicon.

 

• Scandium (Option 2): This corresponds to Mendeleev's "eka-boron".

 

• Titanium (Option 3): A naturally occurring transition metal unrelated to Mendeleev's eka-silicon prediction.

question: The Atal Innovation Mission was launched in year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) was launched by NITI Aayog in 2016 to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in India. (अटल इनोवेशन मिशन — 2016)

 

• It is the Government of India's flagship initiative for creating and promoting a culture of innovation, established under NITI Aayog.

 

• AIM runs programmes such as Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) in schools and Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) to support startups.

 

• It is named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

 

• AIM also runs the Atal New India Challenge and Mentor India programmes to encourage grassroots innovation.

 

NOTE

 

• 2021 (Option 1): Not the launch year; several later phases/extensions of AIM occurred well after 2016.

 

• 2014 (Option 3): Incorrect; NITI Aayog itself was formed only in January 2015.

 

• 2004 (Option 4): Incorrect; far earlier than AIM's actual launch.

question: Ishwari Prasad is credited to have introduced the ________ Gharana of Kathak.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ishwari Prasad is credited with introducing the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak dance in its early period of development at the court of Awadh. (लखनऊ घराना — कथक नृत्य)

 

• The Lucknow Gharana flourished under the patronage of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah and was later carried forward by Thakur Prasad and his sons Bindadin Maharaj and Kalka Prasad.

 

• This gharana is known for its grace (nazakat), subtle expressions (abhinaya), and intricate footwork blended with storytelling.

 

• Kathak has three principal gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras (Varanasi).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jaipur Gharana emphasises vigorous footwork (tatkar) and rhythmic complexity, while the Banaras Gharana is known for its distinct hand movements (hastak) and simpler spins (chakkars).

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, a legendary exponent of Kathak, belonged to the Lucknow Gharana's Kalka-Bindadin lineage.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaipur (Option 1): Known for powerful, vigorous footwork, associated with a different lineage of founders, not Ishwari Prasad.

 

• Raigarh (Option 2): A smaller gharana that developed later under the patronage of the Raigarh princely state, distinct from Ishwari Prasad's lineage.

 

• Banaras (Option 3): Founded by Janakiprasad, known for its unique hand gestures and simpler spins, not linked to Ishwari Prasad.

question: Which essential amino acid enhances calcium absorption and also plays an important role in the formation of collagen?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lysine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lysine is an essential amino acid (must be obtained from the diet) that plays a key role in calcium absorption and collagen formation. (लाइसिन — कैल्शियम अवशोषण)

 

• It helps the body absorb calcium more effectively and reduces the amount excreted through urine, and it works alongside vitamin C to help form collagen, the main structural protein of skin, bones, and connective tissue.

 

• Good dietary sources of lysine include meat, fish, eggs, dairy, and legumes.

 

• Deficiency of lysine can affect growth, tissue repair, and immune function.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Essential amino acids (9 in humans) cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from food; the other eight are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.

 

• Collagen synthesis also critically depends on Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), which acts as a cofactor for the enzymes that stabilise the collagen structure.

 

NOTE

 

• Arginine (Option 1): Important for protein synthesis and nitric oxide production, not specifically linked to calcium absorption/collagen the way lysine is.

 

• Tyrosine (Option 2): A non-essential amino acid; precursor for hormones such as thyroxine and neurotransmitters like dopamine.

 

• Histidine (Option 4): An essential amino acid important for tissue growth, repair, and histamine production, not specifically linked to calcium absorption.

question: Which of the following is an example of an eastern coast port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai Port.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chennai Port, on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal in Tamil Nadu, is a major artificial port on India's eastern coast. (चेन्नई पत्तन — पूर्वी तट)

 

• It is one of the oldest major ports in India (established 1881) and one of the country's principal artificial harbours.

 

• India's major eastern coast ports include Kolkata, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Ennore (Kamarajar), and Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar).

 

• Western coast ports handle a larger share of India's cargo traffic owing to their proximity to Middle Eastern and Western trade routes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kolkata Port (with its Haldia dock complex) is India's oldest operating major port, established in 1870.

 

• Visakhapatnam Port is the deepest landlocked port on India's eastern coast.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai Port (Option 1): Located on India's western coast, on the Arabian Sea.

 

• Mormugao Port (Option 3): Located in Goa on the western coast.

 

• New Mangalore Port (Option 4): Located in Karnataka on the western coast.

question: Who suggested the law that the British Government passed in 1856 to support widow remarriage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar led the campaign that resulted in the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, legalising the remarriage of Hindu widows. (ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर — विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम 1856)

 

• He petitioned the government and mobilised public opinion against the practice of enforced widowhood in 19th-century Bengal.

 

• The Act was passed under Governor-General Lord Canning on 26 July 1856.

 

• Vidyasagar was also a pioneering social reformer and educationist who worked to promote girls' education in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidyasagar also campaigned against child marriage and polygamy, and simplified/modernised the Bengali alphabet primer (Barnaparichay).

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, an earlier reformer, is chiefly credited with the abolition of Sati (Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829), a separate reform.

 

NOTE

 

• Keshub Chandra Sen (Option 1): A Brahmo Samaj leader associated with the Native Marriage Act, 1872 (setting a minimum marriage age), not the 1856 widow remarriage law.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang (Option 3): Founder of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra, a separate reform movement.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 4): Credited with the abolition of Sati in 1829; he died in 1833, before the 1856 Widow Remarriage Act was passed.

question: In 2022, Vinay Mohan Kwatra took charge as the Foreign Secretary of India. Prior to this, he served as the ambassador to which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vinay Mohan Kwatra took charge as India's Foreign Secretary on 1 May 2022, and immediately prior to this appointment he was serving as India's Ambassador to Nepal (2020-2022). (विनय मोहन क्वात्रा — नेपाल राजदूत)

 

• Before Nepal, Kwatra had also served as India's Ambassador to France (2017-2020).

 

• As Foreign Secretary, Kwatra played a key role in India's G20 presidency (2023) and major bilateral engagements.

 

• He succeeded Harsh Vardhan Shringla as Foreign Secretary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• After his tenure as Foreign Secretary ended in mid-2024, Kwatra was appointed India's Ambassador to the United States in August 2024.

 

• The Foreign Secretary is the senior-most civil servant in India's Ministry of External Affairs and head of the Indian Foreign Service.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhutan (Option 1): Not one of Kwatra's postings before becoming Foreign Secretary.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 2): Not one of Kwatra's postings before becoming Foreign Secretary.

 

• Maldives (Option 4): Not one of Kwatra's postings before becoming Foreign Secretary.

question: An organic reaction used to convert an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide using a copper(I) halide catalyst is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sandmeyer reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sandmeyer reaction converts an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide (or nitrile) using a copper(I) halide (CuCl, CuBr) or copper(I) cyanide as catalyst. (सैंडमेयर अभिक्रिया — एरिल हैलाइड निर्माण)

 

• It was discovered by Swiss chemist Traugott Sandmeyer in 1884.

 

• The reaction proceeds through a radical mechanism, replacing the diazonium (-N₂⁺) group with a halogen atom.

 

• It is a key method in organic synthesis for introducing chlorine, bromine, or cyanide groups onto an aromatic ring at a specific position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gattermann reaction is a related, milder variant that uses copper powder with a hydrohalic acid instead of a copper(I) halide salt.

 

• The Balz-Schiemann reaction converts a diazonium salt into an aryl fluoride using fluoroboric acid (HBF₄), without a copper catalyst.

 

NOTE

 

• Finkelstein reaction (Option 1): Converts alkyl chlorides/bromides into alkyl iodides using sodium iodide; unrelated to diazonium salts.

 

• Gattermann reaction (Option 2): A related but distinct method using copper powder with HCl/HBr instead of a copper(I) halide salt.

 

• Balz-Schiemann reaction (Option 4): Used specifically to prepare aryl fluorides via fluoroborate salts, without a copper catalyst.

question: Pulakeshin II assumed the title of ‘Dakshinapatheshvara’ (lord of the south) after defeating which of the following rulers of north India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harshavardhana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pulakeshin II, the greatest ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Badami, defeated Harshavardhana of Kannauj on the banks of the Narmada river (c. 618-619 CE). (पुलकेशिन द्वितीय — हर्षवर्धन को पराजित)

 

• This victory checked Harshavardhana's southward expansion and earned Pulakeshin II the title "Dakshinapatheshvara" (Lord of the South), as recorded in the Aihole inscription of his court poet Ravikirti.

 

• Pulakeshin II ruled from 610 to 642 CE and also received the title "Parameshvara" after this victory.

 

• Harshavardhana was later defeated at Kanauj, one of the best-documented episodes described by the Chinese traveller Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Aihole inscription (634 CE), composed by Ravikirti, is a key epigraphic source for Pulakeshin II's reign and military victories.

 

• Pulakeshin II was ultimately defeated and killed by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I, who captured the Chalukya capital Vatapi (Badami).

 

NOTE

 

• Rudrasena II (Option 1): A Vakataka king who ruled much earlier (4th century CE) and married a Gupta princess (Prabhavatigupta); unrelated to Pulakeshin II's campaigns.

 

• Dhruvasena II (Option 3): A Maitraka ruler of Valabhi, a contemporary linked to Harshavardhana's court, not the ruler Pulakeshin II defeated for this title.

 

• Prabhakarvardhana (Option 4): Harshavardhana's father, an earlier Pushyabhuti ruler, not the ruler defeated by Pulakeshin II.

question: In chess which of the following may move only diagonally?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Bishop.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In chess, the Bishop is the piece that can move only diagonally, any number of unoccupied squares in any diagonal direction. (बिशप — केवल तिरछी चाल)

 

• Each player starts with two bishops, one moving on light squares and the other on dark squares for the entire game, since diagonal movement never changes square colour.

 

• The bishop's value is generally considered comparable to the knight (roughly three pawns).

 

• A pair of bishops working together can control both colour complexes of the board, a strategic idea popularly known as the "bishop pair" advantage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Queen combines the moves of the Rook (straight lines) and Bishop (diagonals), making it the most powerful piece.

 

• The Knight has a unique "L-shaped" move and is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.

 

NOTE

 

• The Knight (Option 2): Moves in an L-shape (two squares in one direction, then one square perpendicular), not diagonally.

 

• The Queen (Option 3): Can move diagonally but also horizontally and vertically — it is not restricted to diagonal-only movement.

 

• The Rook (Option 4): Moves only horizontally or vertically in straight lines, never diagonally.

question: Which famous santoor player was honoured with the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shivkumar Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, the santoor maestro credited with elevating the Kashmiri folk instrument to a classical concert instrument, was honoured with the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998. (शिवकुमार शर्मा — संतूर वादक)

 

• He pioneered the technique of playing complex ragas on the santoor, an instrument traditionally used only for folk music in Kashmir.

 

• He also formed the famous "Shiv-Hari" duo with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, composing music for several Bollywood films.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1991) and Padma Vibhushan (2001), among numerous other awards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award is a prestigious award instituted in Madhya Pradesh in memory of the sarod maestro Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan.

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma passed away in May 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Tarun Bhattacharya (Option 1): Another noted santoor player, but not the recipient of this specific 1998 award.

 

• Satish Vyas (Option 3): A well-known contemporary santoor player, but not this award's 1998 recipient.

 

• Abhay Sopori (Option 4): A younger-generation santoor player from Kashmir, not this award's 1998 recipient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Malaria (i) is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium (d), transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. (मलेरिया — प्लाज्मोडियम)

 

• Diarrhoea (ii) is commonly caused by Rotavirus (c), a leading cause of severe diarrhoeal disease in young children worldwide.

 

• Typhoid (iii) is caused by the bacterium Salmonella (b) (Salmonella typhi), transmitted through contaminated food and water.

 

• Cholera (iv) is caused by the bacterium Vibrio (a) (Vibrio cholerae), also spread through contaminated water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vaccines exist for several of these diseases, including the rotavirus vaccine, typhoid conjugate vaccine, and oral cholera vaccine, all part of India's public health efforts.

 

• Malaria and diarrhoeal diseases remain among the leading causes of child mortality in developing countries, making early diagnosis and sanitation critical.

• Option 4 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly pairs malaria with Vibrio, diarrhoea with Salmonella, and cholera with Plasmodium.

question: In 1910, The United India House at Seattle, USA, was set up by ___________.
option_2: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The United India House was established in 1910 at Seattle, USA, by Indian revolutionaries Tarak Nath Das and G.D. Kumar to organise and support the Indian independence movement among expatriate Indians on the US Pacific coast. (तारकनाथ दास — यूनाइटेड इंडिया हाउस)

 

• Tarak Nath Das had earlier started the militant nationalist journal "Free Hindustan" from Vancouver, later moving its base to Seattle.

 

• G.D. Kumar had earlier established the Swadesh Sevak Home in Vancouver and published the Gurmukhi paper "Swadesh Sevak" to mobilise Indian (mainly Punjabi) settlers.

 

• These organising efforts among the Indian diaspora in North America were direct precursors to the formation of the Ghadar Party in 1913.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ghadar Party was formally founded in 1913 in San Francisco under Sohan Singh Bhakna as its president, building on this earlier organising work.

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma had separately founded India House in London in 1905 to support Indian students and revolutionaries in Britain.

 

NOTE

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma (Option 1): He founded "India House" in London (1905) and the Indian Home Rule Society — a separate organisation from the Seattle-based United India House.

 

• Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki (Option 3): Bengal-based revolutionaries associated with the 1908 Muzaffarpur bombing, unrelated to the Seattle organisation.

 

• VD Savarkar and Ganesh (Option 4): Savarkar was associated with India House in London and the Abhinav Bharat Society, not the United India House in Seattle.

question: Alla Rakha is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Alla Rakha Khan was one of India's most celebrated tabla players, renowned for his accompaniment of Pandit Ravi Shankar on the sitar. (अल्ला रक्खा — तबला वादक)

 

• He developed the Punjab gharana style of tabla playing and helped popularise Indian classical percussion internationally.

 

• His son, Ustad Zakir Hussain, became one of the most famous tabla virtuosos in the world.

 

• Alla Rakha received the Padma Shri in 1982 for his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tabla is a pair of hand drums (a smaller "dayan/tabla" and a larger "bayan"), central to Hindustani classical music accompaniment.

 

• Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha's son, received the Padma Vibhushan (2023) and multiple Grammy Awards for his tabla performances.

 

NOTE

 

• Damaru (Option 1): A small two-headed hand drum associated with Lord Shiva, not Alla Rakha's instrument.

 

• Bansuri (Option 2): A bamboo flute, famously played by artists like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Alla Rakha.

 

• Shehnai (Option 3): A wind instrument famously played by Ustad Bismillah Khan, not Alla Rakha.

question: The record obtained by the measurement of earthquake is called a:
solution_text:
The correct answer is seismogram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The instrument that detects and measures ground motion during an earthquake is called a seismograph, while the actual recorded output/trace it produces is called a seismogram. (भूकंपलेख — सिस्मोग्राम)

 

• A seismogram graphically displays the arrival times and amplitudes of seismic waves (P-waves, S-waves, and surface waves) as recorded by the seismograph.

 

• Seismologists use seismograms to determine the location, magnitude, and depth of an earthquake's focus.

 

• The scientific study of earthquakes and seismic waves is called seismology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The point on the Earth's surface directly above the earthquake's focus is called the epicentre.

 

• The Richter scale, developed in 1935 by Charles F. Richter, was one of the earliest scales used to express earthquake magnitude; it has since been largely supplanted by the moment magnitude scale.

 

NOTE

 

• Seismograph (Option 1): This is the instrument used to detect and record ground motion, not the record itself.

 

• Seismology (Option 3): This is the scientific study of earthquakes and seismic waves, not the record produced.

 

• Seismic wave (Option 4): This refers to the energy waves that travel through the Earth during an earthquake, not the recorded output.

question: Makar Sankranti is the festival dedicated to which of the following Lords?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun God, Surya, marking the sun's transit (sankranti) into the zodiac sign of Makar (Capricorn). (मकर संक्रांति — सूर्य देव)

 

• It is celebrated annually on 14 or 15 January and marks the beginning of the sun's northward journey (Uttarayana).

 

• The festival is celebrated across India under various regional names, such as Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Lohri (Punjab, the eve of Sankranti), Bihu (Assam), and Uttarayan (Gujarat).

 

• It is one of the few Hindu festivals with a fixed date on the solar calendar, unlike most others which follow the lunar calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kite-flying is a well-known tradition associated with Makar Sankranti/Uttarayan, especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan.

 

• Major Kumbh Mela bathing dates are often aligned with Makar Sankranti.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganesha (Option 1): The principal festival dedicated to Lord Ganesha is Ganesh Chaturthi, not Makar Sankranti.

 

• Chandra (Option 3): No major pan-Indian festival is specifically tied to the Moon god in the way Makar Sankranti is tied to Surya.

 

• Indra (Option 4): Indra, king of the gods and god of rain/thunder, is not the deity associated with Makar Sankranti.

question: What is the primary objective of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act of 2006 in India?
option_2: To focus on large-scale industries only
option_3: To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs
option_4: To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006 was enacted to promote, develop, and enhance the competitiveness of micro, small and medium enterprises in India. (एमएसएमई विकास अधिनियम 2006 — प्रोत्साहन एवं विकास)

 

• It provided the first-ever legal framework for recognition of the concept of "enterprise" (covering both manufacturing and service sectors) and classified units as micro, small, and medium based on investment (revised in 2020 to include turnover as well).

 

• The Act established institutions like the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to advise the government on MSME policy.

 

• It also introduced provisions for timely payment to MSME suppliers and set up Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils to resolve payment disputes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the revised (2020) MSME classification, criteria are based on both investment in plant/machinery and annual turnover.

 

• The Ministry of MSME implements schemes such as the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) and the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme to support the sector.

 

NOTE

 

• To regulate foreign companies (Option 1): The MSMED Act deals with domestic micro, small, and medium enterprises, not the regulation of foreign companies.

 

• To focus on large-scale industries only (Option 2): The Act's entire focus is on micro, small, and medium enterprises, explicitly excluding large-scale industry.

 

• To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs (Option 3): The Act does not deal with trade/tariff policy; it provides a development and regulatory framework for MSMEs.

question: NDP = _________.
option_3: GDP – Net factor income from abroad
option_4: GDP + Net factor income from abroad
solution_text:
The correct answer is GDP – Depreciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net Domestic Product (NDP) is obtained by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from Gross Domestic Product (GDP): NDP = GDP – Depreciation. (शुद्ध घरेलू उत्पाद — जीडीपी घटा मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Depreciation accounts for the wearing out/consumption of capital assets (machinery, buildings, etc.) during the production process in a year.

 

• NDP better reflects the actual addition to a nation's wealth in a year, since it excludes the value needed merely to replace worn-out capital.

 

• GDP, in contrast, includes this depreciation and therefore overstates the net increase in the economy's productive capacity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Income (NNP at factor cost) = NDP + Net factor income from abroad – Net indirect taxes.

 

• Gross National Product (GNP) = GDP + Net factor income from abroad (income earned by residents abroad minus income earned by non-residents within the country).

 

NOTE

 

• GDP + Depreciation (Option 2): This is the reverse relationship and does not represent NDP; adding depreciation would only inflate the domestic product figure further.

 

• GDP – Net factor income from abroad (Option 3): This describes an adjustment linking GDP to GNP-type figures via factor income, not the depreciation-based NDP calculation.

 

• GDP + Net factor income from abroad (Option 4): This formula actually defines Gross National Product (GNP), not Net Domestic Product.

question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Election Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part XV.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part XV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 324 to 329) deals with "Elections", including the establishment and powers of the Election Commission of India. (भाग XV — निर्वाचन आयोग)

 

• Article 324 vests the "superintendence, direction and control of elections" in the Election Commission.

 

• The Election Commission is a permanent, independent constitutional body responsible for conducting free and fair elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

 

• Originally a single-member body, it became a multi-member body (Chief Election Commissioner plus two Election Commissioners) after 1989-93.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 325 and 326 provide for a common electoral roll and adult suffrage (voting age reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Amendment, 1988).

 

• The Chief Election Commissioner enjoys security of tenure similar to a Supreme Court judge and can only be removed through impeachment.

 

NOTE

 

• Part XII (Option 2): Deals with "Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits" (Articles 264-300A), not elections.

 

• Part IV (Option 3): Contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51), not elections.

 

• Part XI (Option 4): Deals with "Relations between the Union and the States" (Articles 245-263), not elections.

question: Ghiyas ud-din Balban had set up a _________ department called 'Diwan-i-arz'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is military.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sultan Ghiyas ud-din Balban (r. 1266-1287) of the Delhi Sultanate's Slave (Mamluk) dynasty strengthened royal authority and reorganised the military department, called "Diwan-i-Arz". (दीवान-ए-अर्ज़ — सैन्य विभाग)

 

• The Diwan-i-Arz was responsible for the recruitment, organisation, inspection, and payment of the army.

 

• Balban is also known for his policy of "Blood and Iron" to curb the power of the nobility (the Chahalgani/Group of Forty) and for introducing rigorous court ceremonies such as sijda and paibos to enhance royal prestige.

 

• He was a prominent slave-general (Ilbari Turk) who eventually became Sultan of Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key departments of the Delhi Sultanate administration included the Diwan-i-Wizarat (finance, headed by the Wazir) and Diwan-i-Insha (royal correspondence).

 

• The office of Diwan-i-Arz was later revived and strengthened further by Alauddin Khalji for maintaining a large standing army.

 

NOTE

 

• Commerce (Option 2): Not the function of the Diwan-i-Arz; trade matters were largely governed by market regulations under later rulers like Alauddin Khalji.

 

• Education (Option 3): Not the function of the Diwan-i-Arz department.

 

• Agriculture (Option 4): Revenue and agriculture were typically handled by the Diwan-i-Wizarat, not the Diwan-i-Arz.

question: According to Census of India 2011, female adolescents in the age group of 10-19 years had a share of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 47.3%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the total adolescent (10-19 years) population, female adolescents accounted for a share of about 47.3%, with male adolescents making up the remaining roughly 52.7%. (महिला किशोर — जनगणना 2011)

 

• Adolescents (10-19 years) formed about 20.9% of India's total population as per Census 2011, and within this cohort the female share was 47.3%.

 

• This data is significant for policy planning around adolescent health, nutrition, and education schemes such as the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK).

 

• India has one of the largest adolescent populations of any country in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Programmes like the Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG) and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao specifically target the wellbeing of adolescent girls identified through such census data.

 

• The overall sex ratio recorded in Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males, broadly consistent with a slightly lower female share within the adolescent age cohort as well.

 

NOTE

 

• 52.7% (Option 1): This corresponds to the male share of the adolescent population, not the female share.

 

• 31.3% (Option 3): Does not correspond to any recognised Census 2011 adolescent gender-share figure.

 

• 20.9% (Option 4): This is the approximate share of adolescents (both sexes combined) in India's total population, not the female-specific share within the adolescent cohort.

question: When did a States Reorganisation Commission was set up, which recommended the creation of linguistic States on the basis of larger linguistic groups?
solution_text:
The correct answer is December 1953.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was set up by the Government of India in December 1953, chaired by Justice Fazal Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members. (राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग — दिसंबर 1953)

 

• The Commission was tasked with examining the reorganisation of state boundaries, and it recommended that states be reorganised broadly on the basis of language.

 

• Its report, submitted in 1955, led to the enactment of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which redrew state boundaries largely along linguistic lines.

 

• The formation of Andhra State in 1953 (following Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death) was an immediate precursor that prompted the setting up of this Commission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised India into 14 states and 6 union territories.

 

• Later linguistic reorganisations, such as the bifurcation of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat (1960) and Punjab into Punjab and Haryana (1966), occurred even after the 1956 Act.

 

NOTE

 

• December 1963 (Option 1): Not the year the Commission was set up.

 

• December 1956 (Option 3): Close to when the States Reorganisation Act came into effect (1 November 1956), not when the Commission was constituted.

 

• December 1958 (Option 4): Not connected to the setting up of the States Reorganisation Commission.

question: Which of the following is associated with the retreating monsoon in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is October heat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "October heat" refers to the oppressive, sultry weather conditions experienced in parts of India during October, when the monsoon retreats and skies become clear. (अक्टूबर हीट — मानसून की वापसी)

 

• As the southwest monsoon withdraws from northern India (beginning around September), reduced cloud cover and calm winds allow daytime temperatures and humidity to rise again, producing this uncomfortable "October heat".

 

• It occurs during the transition period known as the retreating/post-monsoon season (October-November).

 

• This period is also associated with occasional cyclonic storms in the Bay of Bengal, which can bring heavy rainfall to India's south-eastern coast (Tamil Nadu) via the northeast monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The northeast (retreating) monsoon brings the bulk of Tamil Nadu's annual rainfall between October and December.

 

• India's monsoon-related seasons are broadly classified as: cold weather season (winter), hot weather season (summer), southwest monsoon (rainy) season, and the retreating/post-monsoon season.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahawat (Option 1): Winter rainfall in northwest India caused by western disturbances originating in the Mediterranean, occurring in the cold season, unrelated to monsoon retreat.

 

• Kaal Baisakhi (Option 2): Pre-monsoon (April-May) thunderstorms in West Bengal and Assam, associated with the onset, not the retreat, of the monsoon.

 

• Loo (Option 4): Hot, dry summer winds that blow over north and northwest India before the monsoon's onset (May-June), not during its retreat.

question: Where was the Durand Cup Tournament started in India in 1888?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shimla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Durand Cup, Asia's oldest football tournament and one of the oldest in the world, was started in 1888 at Shimla, then the summer capital of British India. (डूरंड कप — शिमला, 1888)

 

• It was founded by Sir Mortimer Durand, the Foreign Secretary of British India, after whom the tournament (and separately, the Durand Line) is named.

 

• It was originally intended as a tournament for British Indian Army units and was first known as the "Durand Football Tournament".

 

• Today, the Durand Cup is jointly organised in Kolkata by the Indian Army, the Government of West Bengal, and the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Durand Cup trophy set consists of three cups: the Durand Cup, the Shimla Trophy, and the President's Cup.

 

• Mortimer Durand is also known for demarcating the Durand Line, the boundary between British India (later Pakistan) and Afghanistan, in 1893.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai (Option 1): Not the city where the Durand Cup was first held.

 

• Calcutta (Option 2): The Durand Cup is now hosted primarily in Kolkata (Calcutta), but this is not where it originated in 1888.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Not the city where the Durand Cup was first held.
